title.en: Hertz sphere contact patch and elastic approach

summary: Link sphere approach, repulsive load and a growing pressure patch in a bounded elastic-contact model.
objective: Expose the authoritative model and its visible response: hertz sphere contact patch and elastic approach.
applies_when: Two homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic spheres in frictionless nonadhesive quasi-static normal contact; circular contact radius is much smaller than either sphere radius.
intent_signals: Link sphere approach, repulsive load and a growing pressure patch in a bounded elastic-contact model.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable demonstration of hertz sphere contact patch and elastic approach with parameter controls and a reset.
negative_signals: Not adhesion, plastic indentation, rough surfaces, tangential friction, impact damping or a complete displacement-field solver.
not_for: Not adhesion, plastic indentation, rough surfaces, tangential friction, impact damping or a complete displacement-field solver.

principles: The load law computes an elastic response to prescribed approach; it does not simulate impact or dissipate energy.
Use actual model metres for contact calculations; an enlarged inset is a display transform.
implementation: Own positive radii RA,RB in m, Young moduli EA,EB in Pa and stable isotropic Poisson ratios -1<nuA,nuB<0.5. Set 1/Rstar=1/RA+1/RB and 1/Estar=(1-nuA^2)/EA+(1-nuB^2)/EB. For approach delta>0, a=sqrt(Rstar*delta) and F=(4/3)*Estar*sqrt(Rstar)*delta^(3/2) in N.
For separated or just-touching state delta<=0 set F=0 and omit the patch. For delta>0 show p(rho)=3F/(2*pi*a*a)*sqrt(1-rho*rho/(a*a)) only for 0<=rho<=a; zero outside. Guard the zero-load division.

Vary approach or modulus and derive load, patch and labels together. Show the approach of distant undeformed references; two overlapping undeformed spheres are only a schematic, not a resolved deformation field. Use an optional pressure-disk inset and state its magnification. Expose a/RA and a/RB so invalid small-contact regimes are visible.
observable_checks: Multiplying positive delta by four multiplies a by two and F by eight at fixed materials and radii.
Integrating displayed axisymmetric pressure gives F; pressure vanishes at the edge. At separation there is neither tensile force nor a residual patch.

known_limits: Not adhesion, plastic indentation, rough surfaces, tangential friction, impact damping or a complete displacement-field solver.
Authored reusable guidance; no solver or rendered artifact has been tested for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a cutaway, restrained ghost reference or annotated section only when it clarifies the modeled relation; a planar diagram remains valid when depth adds no information.

claims.statement: For small frictionless elastic sphere contact, effective radius and modulus determine a=(3FRstar/(4Estar))^(1/3), approach delta=a^2/Rstar and pressure p(rho)=3F/(2*pi*a^2)*sqrt(1-rho^2/a^2). Eliminating a gives F proportional to delta^(3/2).
claims.scope: Two homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic spheres in frictionless nonadhesive quasi-static normal contact; circular contact radius is much smaller than either sphere radius.

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4.10 Frictionless contact between two elastic spheres; relations between P,h,a and contact pressure
